title: What is one sixth plus one third?
description: One sixth and one third are added by keeping one sixth as it is and rewriting one third as two sixths. The sum three sixths is then written in lowest terms. Keeko doubts the answer by adding the tops and adding the bottoms.
teaching_notes: One idea: when one bottom number goes into the other, only one fraction needs rewriting. Then write the sum in lowest terms. Watch for the slip of adding the bottoms.

video_script.why: A learner adds fractions when one bottom number goes into the other, and writes the sum in lowest terms.
video_script.substitution: the book's own sum one sixth plus one third
video_script.anchor: two strips of the same length, one cut into six equal parts and one cut into three
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the tops and adds the bottoms and gets two ninths. Two ninths is smaller than one third alone, so the idea is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: one sixth and one third make one half

final_answer.spoken: one sixth and one third make one half

video_script.fraction_reading: one sixth, one third, two sixths, three sixths, one half, two ninths
never_show: two ninths written as the sum before Keeko's doubt
maths_rules: the smallest common multiple of 6 and 3 is 6, so 1/6 stays 1/6
lowest terms: 3/6 = (3 / 3)/(6 / 3) = 1/2, dividing by 3, the biggest common factor of 3 and 6
slip: Keeko adds the tops and the bottoms and gets 2/9; 2/9 < 1/3, which is one of the parts
video_script.design: Two strips of the same length, in sixths and in thirds, stay on the board. One third is cut in half into two sixths, then the sixths are counted and the sum is simplified.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; two strips of the same length, one cut into 6 equal parts with 1 shaded in teal and one cut into 3 equal parts with 1 shaded in amber; the words sum? appear

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.strips: two strips of the same length appear, cut in sixths and in thirds, with one part shaded on each
marks.ask: the words sum? appear between the strips

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is from your book, and it asks for the sum of one sixth and one third.
<bookmark mark='strips'/>Sixths and thirds are different fractional units.

beats.on_screen: the two strips hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the third-strip is cut in half into two sixths; the note 6 is a multiple of 3 appears; the words lowest terms appear with the note no common factor except 1

marks.multiple: each third of the strip is cut in half and the note six is a multiple of three appears
marks.terms: the words lowest terms appear with the note top and bottom share no factor except one

narration: <bookmark mark='multiple'/>Six is already a multiple of three, so every third can be cut into sixths.
<bookmark mark='terms'/>Lowest terms means that the top and the bottom numbers share no factor except one.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the two fractions are one sixth and one third.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum of 1/6 and 1/3, in lowest terms
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the sum of the two fractions in lowest terms.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the smallest common multiple of 6 and 3 is 6, so 1/6 stays 1/6

marks.six: the smallest common multiple 6 is written
marks.stay: 1/6 is boxed and the words stays as it is appear

narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Step one, the smallest common multiple of six and three is six.
<bookmark mark='stay'/>The bottom number of one sixth is already six, so one sixth stays as it is.

marks.mul: the top and the bottom of 1/3 are multiplied by 2

narration: <bookmark mark='mul'/>Step two, multiply the top and the bottom of one third by two.
<bookmark mark='res'/>One times two over three times two is two sixths.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: both in sixths; add the numerators: 1 + 2 = 3 sixths, that is 3/6

marks.add: the shaded sixths of both strips slide together and 1 + 2 = 3 sixths is written

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, both fractions are in sixths, so we add the numerators. One plus two is three, which gives three sixths.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: lowest terms: divide the top and the bottom of 3/6 by 3, the biggest common factor of 3 and 6

marks.div: the top and the bottom of 3/6 are divided by 3

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step four, three sixths is not in lowest terms. Divide the top and the bottom by three, the biggest common factor of three and six.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Dividing both numbers by three gives one over two, so one sixth and one third make one half.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two strips
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says add the tops and add the bottoms: 2/9; a strip of 9 equal parts with 2 shaded sits under the one third strip and is shorter; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears
marks.short: a strip of nine equal parts with two shaded sits under the one third strip and is shorter

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks they make two ninths, because one plus one is two and six plus three is nine.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Two ninths is smaller than one third alone, and adding cannot leave us with less.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>We make the fractional units the same first, and then we add.
